newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-LUYENDYK WINS HIS SECOND INDY 500.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-LUYENDYK WINS HIS SECOND INDY 500.

text.p: Arie Luyendyk earned his second Indianapolis 500 title on Tuesday, getting past his Treadway Racing teammate Scott Goodyear with seven laps to go and hanging on through the checkered flag.
Luyendyk, who pocketed a prize in excess of $1 million, led Goodyear, rookie Jeff Ward, Buddy Lazier and Tony Stewart across the finish line as the race ended in controversy.

There were three caution flags during the final 12 laps, the last apparently as a result of Stewart -- a contender throughout -- slapping the wall coming out of turn four. Stewart remained in the race as one of five cars remaining on the lead lap.
As the cars came to restart the race on the final lap, the green flag was waved but the lights along the 2 1/2-mile (4-km) oval that alert the drivers to the track condition remained yellow.
Goodyear, involved in a controversial finish during Jacques Villeneueve's 1995 victory, had no chance of making a run on Luyendyk as a result.
The race was finally run on Tuesday after aborted efforts to run the 81st edition of the classic on Sunday and Monday at Indianapolis Motor Speedway.
Rain ruined any chance to start the race as scheduled on Sunday. The event was stopped after just 15 laps of the 200-lap race on Monday when rains returned.
It was a repeat success for Luyendyk and a repeat disappointment for Goodyear.
The Dutchman also triumphed in 1990, while the Canadian was runner-up once before. In 1992, Goodyear finished 0.043 of a second behind Al Unser Jr. in the closest finish in event history.
In 1995, Goodyear was leading late in the race, but was penalised two laps for passing the pace car during a restart. That opened the way for fellow-Canadian Jacques Villeneuve to win.
The race began with 29 cars lined up single file in the order they were running. Six cars did not take the restart.

The first three laps Tuesday were under the yellow caution flag to give the cars and their unproven engines longer to warm up. Stewart stayed in the lead when the green came out, but the yellow was displayed moments later when Robby Gordon's car caught fire.

Gordon pulled off the track, jumped out of the car and began rolling on the infield grass as the invisible methanol flames started burning the right leg of his uniform. Crews quickly extinguished the flames and the car was brought back to the pits, out of the race.
Gordon was treated in the infield medical centre for burns on his right hand, wrist and thigh and left wrist.
